items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall that we use sigma notation to write sums concisely. For example,

Content:
[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n a_i]

Content:
refers to the sum of all terms in the sequence [MATH: a_i,] where the index [MATH: i] ranges from [MATH: 1] to [MATH: n\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^n a_i = a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n]

Content:
Sigma notation can also represent sums whose terms depend on two indices. That is, double sums of the form

Content:
[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}]
where [MATH: i] ranges from [MATH: 1] to [MATH: m,] and [MATH: j] ranges from [MATH: 1] to [MATH: n\mathbin.] Thus, a double summation is just a "sum of a sum."

Content:
In calculating double summations, we follow two steps:

Content:
- First, we evaluate the inner sum by fixing the index of the outer sum ([MATH: i]) and incrementing only the inner index ([MATH: j]).
- Next, we evaluate the outer sum by incrementing the outer sum index.

Content:
To illustrate how it works, suppose we are given the following double sum:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j=1}^4 (i+j)]

Content:
To compute this double sum, we can proceed as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(2)∑_(j = 1)^(4)(i + j)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(2)[(∑_(j = 1)^(4)(i + j))]; = ∑_(i = 1)^(2)[(i + 1) + (i + 2) + (i + 3) + (i + 4)]; = ∑_(i = 1)^(2)(4i + 10); = 4(1) + 10 + 4(2) + 10; = 4 + 10 + 8 + 10; = 32]

Content:
Later, we will provide some formulas that will help us simplify many double summations calculations.

items.title: Computing a Double Summation

sections.normalized_html: Evaluate [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^3\sum_{i=1}^2 (i+j).]
sections.readable_text: Evaluate [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^3\sum_{i=1}^2 (i+j).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we write out the inner summation by summing over the index [MATH: i\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(3)∑_(i = 1)^(2)(i + j)|= ∑_(j = 1)^(3)[∑_(i = 1)^(2)(i + j)]; = ∑_(j = 1)^(3)[(1 + j) + (2 + j)]; = ∑_(j = 1)^(3)(3 + 2j)]

Then, we calculate the sum above by summing over the index [MATH: j\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(3)(3 + 2j)|= (3 + 2 ⋅ 1) + (3 + 2 ⋅ 2) + (3 + 2 ⋅ 3); = 5 + 7 + 9; = 21]

Content:
Double summations satisfy the following properties:

Content:
The Constant Multiple Rule

Content:
We can factor out a constant multiple from a double summation:
[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n k a_{ij} = k\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}]

Content:
The Sum Rule

Content:
We can distribute a double summation over a sum of terms.
[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (a_{ij} + b_{ij}) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij} + \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n b_{ij}]

Content:
The Double Sum of Units

Content:
Recall that for single summations, we have

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{j=1}^{n} 1 = \underbrace{1+1+\cdots+1}_{n\textrm{ times}} = n.]

Content:
Analogously for double summations, we have that

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 1 = mn.]

items.title: Applying the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules

sections.normalized_html:
Find the value of the double sum

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} (1+2a_{ij}-b_{ij})]

given that

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} a_{ij} = 8, \qquad\sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} b_{ij} = 15.]
sections.readable_text:
Find the value of the double sum

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} (1+2a_{ij}-b_{ij})]

given that

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} a_{ij} = 8, \qquad\sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} b_{ij} = 15.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)(a_{ij} + b_{ij})|= ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)a_{ij} + ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)b_{ij},; ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)ka_{ij}|= k∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)a_{ij}.]

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)(1 + 2a_{ij} − b_{ij})|= ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1 + ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)2a_{ij} − ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)b_{ij}; = (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 2∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)a_{ij} − ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)b_{ij}; = (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 2(8) − 15; = (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 1.]

Now, using the fact that

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 1 = mn,]

we have

[MATH: (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 1|= 5 ⋅ 8 + 1; = 40 + 1; = 41.]

So, we conclude that

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} (1+2a_{ij}-b_{ij}) = 41.]

items.title: Applying the Product Rule and Swap Rules

sections.normalized_html:
Find the value of the double sum

[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{15} \sum_{j=1}^{18} (a_{i} - 2)( b_{j}+1)]

given that

[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{15}a_i = 40, \qquad \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^{18}b_j =-8 .]
sections.readable_text:
Find the value of the double sum

[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{15} \sum_{j=1}^{18} (a_{i} - 2)( b_{j}+1)]

given that

[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{15}a_i = 40, \qquad \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^{18}b_j =-8 .]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The product rule for double summations states that

[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{i}b_j = \sum_{i=1}^m a_i \sum_{j=1}^n b_{j}.]

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(15)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(a_{i} − 2)(b_{j} + 1)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(15)(a_{i} − 2)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(b_{j} + 1).]

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(15)(a_{i} − 2)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(b_{j} + 1)|= (∑_(i = 1)^(15)a_{i} − ∑_(i = 1)^(15)2) ⋅ (∑_(j = 1)^(18)b_{j} + ∑_(j = 1)^(18)1); = (∑_(i = 1)^(15)a_{i} − 2∑_(i = 1)^(15)1) ⋅ (∑_(j = 1)^(18)b_{j} + ∑_(j = 1)^(18)1); = (40 − 2 ⋅ 15) ⋅ (− 8 + 18); = (10) ⋅ (10); = 100.]
sections.readable_text:
The product rule for double summations states that

[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{i}b_j = \sum_{i=1}^m a_i \sum_{j=1}^n b_{j}.]

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(15)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(a_{i} − 2)(b_{j} + 1)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(15)(a_{i} − 2)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(b_{j} + 1).]

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(15)(a_{i} − 2)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(b_{j} + 1)|= (∑_(i = 1)^(15)a_{i} − ∑_(i = 1)^(15)2) ⋅ (∑_(j = 1)^(18)b_{j} + ∑_(j = 1)^(18)1); = (∑_(i = 1)^(15)a_{i} − 2∑_(i = 1)^(15)1) ⋅ (∑_(j = 1)^(18)b_{j} + ∑_(j = 1)^(18)1); = (40 − 2 ⋅ 15) ⋅ (− 8 + 18); = (10) ⋅ (10); = 100.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Recall that we use sigma notation to write sums concisely. For example,

Content:
[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n a_i]

Content:
refers to the sum of all terms in the sequence [MATH: a_i,] where the index [MATH: i] ranges from [MATH: 1] to [MATH: n\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^n a_i = a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n]

Content:
Sigma notation can also represent sums whose terms depend on two indices. That is, double sums of the form

Content:
[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}]
where [MATH: i] ranges from [MATH: 1] to [MATH: m,] and [MATH: j] ranges from [MATH: 1] to [MATH: n\mathbin.] Thus, a double summation is just a "sum of a sum."

Content:
In calculating double summations, we follow two steps:

Content:
- First, we evaluate the inner sum by fixing the index of the outer sum ([MATH: i]) and incrementing only the inner index ([MATH: j]).
- Next, we evaluate the outer sum by incrementing the outer sum index.

Content:
To illustrate how it works, suppose we are given the following double sum:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j=1}^4 (i+j)]

Content:
To compute this double sum, we can proceed as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(2)∑_(j = 1)^(4)(i + j)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(2)[(∑_(j = 1)^(4)(i + j))]; = ∑_(i = 1)^(2)[(i + 1) + (i + 2) + (i + 3) + (i + 4)]; = ∑_(i = 1)^(2)(4i + 10); = 4(1) + 10 + 4(2) + 10; = 4 + 10 + 8 + 10; = 32]

Content:
Later, we will provide some formulas that will help us simplify many double summations calculations.

---

Item 2 — Example: Computing a Double Summation

Example Prompt:
Evaluate [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^3\sum_{i=1}^2 (i+j).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we write out the inner summation by summing over the index [MATH: i\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(3)∑_(i = 1)^(2)(i + j)|= ∑_(j = 1)^(3)[∑_(i = 1)^(2)(i + j)]; = ∑_(j = 1)^(3)[(1 + j) + (2 + j)]; = ∑_(j = 1)^(3)(3 + 2j)]

Then, we calculate the sum above by summing over the index [MATH: j\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(3)(3 + 2j)|= (3 + 2 ⋅ 1) + (3 + 2 ⋅ 2) + (3 + 2 ⋅ 3); = 5 + 7 + 9; = 21]

---

Item 5 — Tutorial: The Sum and Constant Multiple Rules

Content:
Double summations satisfy the following properties:

Content:
The Constant Multiple Rule

Content:
We can factor out a constant multiple from a double summation:
[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n k a_{ij} = k\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}]

Content:
The Sum Rule

Content:
We can distribute a double summation over a sum of terms.
[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (a_{ij} + b_{ij}) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij} + \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n b_{ij}]

Content:
The Double Sum of Units

Content:
Recall that for single summations, we have

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{j=1}^{n} 1 = \underbrace{1+1+\cdots+1}_{n\textrm{ times}} = n.]

Content:
Analogously for double summations, we have that

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 1 = mn.]

---

Item 6 — Example: Applying the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules

Example Prompt:
Find the value of the double sum

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} (1+2a_{ij}-b_{ij})]

given that

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} a_{ij} = 8, \qquad\sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} b_{ij} = 15.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)(a_{ij} + b_{ij})|= ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)a_{ij} + ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)b_{ij},; ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)ka_{ij}|= k∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)a_{ij}.]

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)(1 + 2a_{ij} − b_{ij})|= ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1 + ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)2a_{ij} − ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)b_{ij}; = (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 2∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)a_{ij} − ∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)b_{ij}; = (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 2(8) − 15; = (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 1.]

Now, using the fact that

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 1 = mn,]

we have

[MATH: (∑_(i = 1)^(5)∑_(j = 1)^(8)1) + 1|= 5 ⋅ 8 + 1; = 40 + 1; = 41.]

So, we conclude that

[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^{5} \sum_{j=1}^{8} (1+2a_{ij}-b_{ij}) = 41.]

Item 9 — Tutorial: The Product and Swap Rules

Content:
In addition, we have the following useful rules:

Content:
The Product Rule

Content:
We can distribute a double summation over a product of single-index terms with different indices.
[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{i}b_j = \sum_{i=1}^m a_i \sum_{j=1}^n b_{j}]

Content:
The Swap Rule

Content:
We can swap the order of summations in a double summation.
[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}= \sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ij}]

---

Item 10 — Example: Applying the Product Rule and Swap Rules

Example Prompt:
Find the value of the double sum

[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{15} \sum_{j=1}^{18} (a_{i} - 2)( b_{j}+1)]

given that

[MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{15}a_i = 40, \qquad \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^{18}b_j =-8 .]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The product rule for double summations states that

[MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{i}b_j = \sum_{i=1}^m a_i \sum_{j=1}^n b_{j}.]

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(15)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(a_{i} − 2)(b_{j} + 1)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(15)(a_{i} − 2)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(b_{j} + 1).]

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(15)(a_{i} − 2)∑_(j = 1)^(18)(b_{j} + 1)|= (∑_(i = 1)^(15)a_{i} − ∑_(i = 1)^(15)2) ⋅ (∑_(j = 1)^(18)b_{j} + ∑_(j = 1)^(18)1); = (∑_(i = 1)^(15)a_{i} − 2∑_(i = 1)^(15)1) ⋅ (∑_(j = 1)^(18)b_{j} + ∑_(j = 1)^(18)1); = (40 − 2 ⋅ 15) ⋅ (− 8 + 18); = (10) ⋅ (10); = 100.]
